references.text: God establishes his covenant with Noah and commands him to enter the ark with his family. This is mirrored by the command to leave the ark in Gen 8:16.
God commands Noah to enter the ark with his entire household, which is a direct parallel to the command to leave the ark in Gen 8:16.
Noah and his family enter the ark to escape the flood, which is directly related to their exit from the ark in Gen 8:16.
Noah, his three sons, his wife, and his three sons' wives entered the ark—the same people commanded to go out in Gen 8:16.
Noah, his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives went out of the ark—the immediate fulfillment of God's command in Gen 8:16.
God blesses Noah and his sons after they have left the ark, which follows directly after the command in Gen 8:16.
God commands Noah and his family to be fruitful and multiply on the earth, which is a consequence of their leaving the ark following the command in Gen 8:16.
9:10 unfolds the theological significance of the exit in 8:16 by extending the covenant to include all living things, not just humans.
